Definition: from G4314 and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await:--(be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.
BiblicalUsage: Prosdokao means to look for, to expect, whether in hope or in fear. The people wondered whether John was the Christ, and John sent to ask Jesus, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? Peter tells believers to look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness, and to be diligent to be found of Him in peace.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that expectation is the shape of faith: John looked for the Coming One, and we look for the new heavens, and both waitings end in the same Person. I believe the way to wait is diligence, not daydreaming, because the day we look for will find us as we are.
